# PR #3321: Patch (part 3 of 3): Open all packs and saving several decks are one request each

Closes #3212

## What changed

**Open all is one request** (`POST /api/packs/open-all`, ruling R3212000)
- **Request.** The body is `{ pack, count }`. `count` must be a whole number from 1 to `PACKS_OPEN_ALL_MAX` (20); anything else is a 400.
- **Spend rules.** It is one spend:
  - it waits for the account's spend turn (R2378000);
  - it runs under the account's economy lock (R1301003);
  - it takes an optional `Idempotency-Key` stored under its own route (R2124000);
  - it answers 409 while `ECONOMY_LIVE` is off.
- **Same rolls as single opens.** The server reads the account's records once. Each pack then rolls from its own fresh server seed on what the previous pack left (`records_after`). The result matches the same number of single opens with the same seeds: cards, pity, bars, ledger rows and their order, and each row's `ref` holds its own opening's log. The only difference is that the whole batch shares one timestamp.
- **All or nothing.** If fewer packs are held than asked, it answers 409 before writing anything.
- **Fixed number of writes.** Everything is written by `write_grants_all`: one statement each for inventory and cosmetics and counters, and two for the collection (quantities and ledger rows). The number of statements does not grow with the count.
- **New store methods**, in Postgres and the in-memory fake:
  - `economy_inventory_write_all` and `economy_counters_write_all` check the running total in grant order (a window `min` in Postgres). So a batch is refused exactly when one grant at a time would be refused.
  - `economy_cosmetics_grant_all` refuses a cosmetic already owned, a pair listed twice, a clear, or a second account.
- **Answer.** `{ openings }`, each exactly what `POST /api/packs/open` answers.
- **Shop.** Open all sends one request for `min(held, 20)` packs and labels the button with that number. It then shows the packs one at a time without sending anything more, and folds only the last opening into its panels (R3211000).

**Deck autosave is one request per pass** (`POST /api/decks/sync`, ruling R3212001)
- **Request.** The body is `{ decks, trios, deletedTrios, deletedDecks }`, at most `DECK_SYNC_ITEMS_MAX` (30) items in all; more is a 400 and nothing runs.
- **Each item as its own route.** The server runs deck saves, then trio saves, then trio deletions, then deck deletions. Each one goes through the same code as its own `PUT` or `DELETE`: I moved those handlers' bodies into `save_deck`, `save_trio`, `remove_deck` and `remove_trio`, and each runs in its own transaction.
- **A refused item refuses alone.** It is answered as `{ id, status, error }`, exactly what its own route would answer, and the rest still save. A server error (5xx) on any item fails the whole request.
- **Client.** `sync.ts` sends one request per pass and handles each item's outcome as it handled that item's own request before.

The single routes stay for older open tabs. Spec changes: two ruling notes, `spec/pending/3212.md`, and small edits to §14.3, the §14 constants table, §9.4, R2124000, R2378000 and R256. Both READMEs now list the routes.

## How I tested it (all run in this session)
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r3212000`: 5 passed. When I broke `records_after` on purpose, the "N opens = Open all of N" test failed.
- Deck route tests (`-- api::decks`): 72 passed, including the 4 R3212001 tests.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store r3212000`: the 2 store cases pass on the fake.
- `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`: 3 shards (228, 228, 227 passed), 0 failed. Both R3212000 store cases ran against Postgres.
- Full `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`: 18518 passed, 0 failed, and no unstaged changes under `apps/web/src/wire`.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`, `catalog check` and `patches check`: all ok.
- Web:
  - the touched test files: 22 files, 593 tests passed;
  - `typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e`, and `tsc` for e2e and the component specs: clean;
  - the harness's `vitest --changed origin/main` command: 413 files, 7939 tests passed.
- **The harness's web command failed on its first run.** It ran while the full cargo build was compiling, was stopped at its 10-minute limit, and reported timeouts in 5 files (wording, patch diff, i18n, landing page, GIF export). Those 5 files pass on their own (104 tests), and the full command then passed.
- **Not checked: `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`.** It needs a `--parent-bin` I didn't build. It diffs against `HEAD`, which is still the earlier work-in-progress commit until the merge of `main` is committed. So it currently shows `main`'s own CSS changes under `apps/web/src/cards/` in reverse, and reports a card-look change. CI's `rust (classify)` will run it on the real commit.

## Decisions the issue didn't settle
- **The sync's 5xx rule.** A refused item (4xx) is answered alone and the rest still save. Rejected: all or nothing, because one bad draft would block every other edit. A server error on any item fails the whole request; items saved before it stay saved, and saving them again on retry changes nothing.
- **One transaction per sync item.** Rejected: one transaction for the whole request, because a refusal raised by the database aborts the entire Postgres transaction.
- **Open all is all or nothing**, not "up to `count`". Rejected because the answer would then depend on the stored state rather than the request.
- **The cap is 20.** Rejected 50: every ledger row carries its opening's log (tens of KB), and all of them are bound into one statement.
- **Only Open all has the economy-off 409**, because the acceptance asks for it. The single open has no such gate today, and I left it alone; the switch is on, so players see no difference.
- **A refused batch uses the single open's words.** It answers with the refusal of its first grant that takes something away, which is the single open's 409 "no unopened pack of that kind".
- **A refused sync request is retried later as a temporary failure** (for example a 404 from a server that predates the route), since no item was judged.
- **Closing the scene partway through an Open all** leaves the rest of the batch opened but not shown. They were already opened and granted in the one spend, so their cards are in the collection.
- **Server README count.** The "one spend at a time" paragraph said "seven" economy spends, which was already out of date. I corrected it to nine.

## Worth a second look
- The three Postgres batch statements in `economy/store.rs` (they update existing rows and insert new ones separately, because Postgres checks a proposed upsert row against `count >= 0` before the conflict). The Postgres suite covers them.
- `sync_answer` in `api/decks.rs` and the rewritten `pass()` in `sync.ts`.

# #3212: Patch (part 3 of 3): Open all packs and saving several decks are one request each
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What it does

Goal (tracker #3203): less compute, better security, faster traffic. Claim all's batch route (Jlore-Studios/JackiOh#3191, R3191000) is the pattern: one spend, one transaction, set-based SQL, each item still its own ledger row.

**Today**, verified on 2026-11-05:

- Each pack open is one `POST /api/packs/open`.
- Deck sync (`apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/sync.ts`) sends one PUT per dirty deck and trio, and one DELETE per deletion, one after another (R256's idempotent saves).

**Change.**

1. **Open all.** One spend opens a named count of one pack kind, up to a new named cap (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
   - It runs in the account's turn (R2378000), under its economy lock (R1301003) and an optional `Idempotency-Key` (R2124000).
   - Each pack rolls exactly as one open does today: the same seeds, draw order, pity and ledger rows (R1301003 and the pack rulings).
   - Writes go in batches where the order allows; the statements must not grow with the count.
   - The answer holds every pack's result.
2. **Save several decks at once.** One request saves the dirty decks and trios and applies the deletions, each as idempotent as its PUT or DELETE today (R256).
   - Each item is checked as today.
   - A refused item refuses as it does alone. Decide and rule whether the rest still save.
3. **Keep the single routes** for older open tabs (CLAUDE.md rule 13).

**Security:** every check one open or one save makes stays, server-side. Nothing the client sends chooses an outcome: counts and items are checked, and the rolls are the server's.

### Acceptance

- Server tests:
  - Open all of N equals N opens, for the same seed and state (cards, pity, ledger rows), on both stores (the store contract);
  - the statements don't grow with N;
  - the key replays;
  - the turn and the economy-off refusals hold.
- Client tests: the shop sends one request for Open all; deck sync sends one request for several dirty items.
- A ruling note in this issue's block, with its tests.
- `crates/server/README.md` lists the routes.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `typecheck` and `eslint` pass.

     - `false` when any is owned already, writing nothing.

3. **`mod pg`.** One statement per method, after `run_as`, binding as `inventory_grant_all` does, read with `query_scalar::<_, bool>`.
   - **Inventory:**
   ```sql
   with g as (select * from unnest($2::text[], $3::text[], $4::int8[], $5::text[], $6::text[], $7::boolean[], $8::int8[])
                with ordinality as g(item, key, delta, reason, ref, dev, at, n)),
   s as (select item, key, sum(delta)::bigint as delta from g group by item, key),
   h as (select s.*, i.count from s left join public.inventory i
           on i.profile_id = $1::uuid and i.item = s.item and i.key = s.key),
   ok as (select coalesce(bool_and(coalesce(count, 0) + delta >= 0), true) as fits from h),
   moved as (update public.inventory i set count = i.count + h.delta from h, ok
              where ok.fits and h.count is not null and i.profile_id = $1::uuid and i.item = h.item and i.key = h.key),
   added as (insert into public.inventory (profile_id, item, key, count)
              select $1::uuid, item, key, delta from h, ok where ok.fits and h.count is null
              on conflict (profile_id, item, key) do update set count = public.inventory.count + excluded.count),
   rows as (insert into public.inventory_grants (profile_id, item, key, delta, reason, ref, dev, at)
             select $1::uuid, item, key, delta, reason, ref, dev, to_timestamp(at::double precision / 1000.0)
               from g, ok where ok.fits order by n)
   select fits from ok
   ```

     1. inventory (`false` → 409 `"no unopened pack of that kind"`);
     2. `collection_upsert_quantities` and `collection_append_grants`, when non-empty;
     3. cosmetics (`false` → `ApiError::internal`);
     4. counters (`false` → `ApiError::internal`).

   - `async fn records_of(tx, profile_id, pack) -> Result<PackRecords, ApiError>`, from lines 165–176.

   - `pub async fn open_pack_in(tx: &mut Tx<'_>, profile_id: &str, inputs: &PackInputs, seed: &str, at: i64) -> Result<OpenedPack, ApiError>`: records, roll, `write_grants` and the answer; the caller holds the lock.
   - `open_pack_once` calls `open_pack_in` between `replayed` and `keep`.

7. **`fn records_after(records: &mut PackRecords, pack: PackKind, opening: &PackOpening)`.**
   - `held += delta` for the inventory grant of `pack.inventory()`.
   - `owned.insert(card_id, quantity)` for each `Cards` entry.
   - Each `Cosmetic` is pushed to `cosmetics.cards` or `cosmetics.account`.
   - `counters.pity = opening.pity`.
   - Bar, cycle and shard counter grants add their delta.
   - The roll only looks these up, so their order does not matter.

8. **`pub async fn open_packs_in(tx, profile_id, inputs, seeds: &[String], at) -> Result<Vec<OpenedPack>, ApiError>`.**
   - Call `records_of` once.
   - For each seed: `open_card_pack(&records, inputs, seed, at).map_err(refused)?`, so too few packs held is a 409 before any write. Then `records_after`, then `OpenedPack { unopened: records.held, .. }`.
   - Finish with `write_grants_all`; each opening's `ref` is its `serde_json::to_string(&opening.log)?`.

   - `pub struct OpenedPacks { pub openings: Vec<OpenedPack> }`, with the same derives as `OpenedPack`.

   - `pub async fn open_packs(..)` is `..once(.., None).now()`.

    - `fn count_of(body) -> Result<usize, ApiError>`: an integer in `1..=PACKS_OPEN_ALL_MAX`, else 400 `"\"count\" must be a whole number from 1 to {PACKS_OPEN_ALL_MAX}"`.
    - `post_open_all`, in this order:
      1. `caller_profile`;
      2. `!app.economy_live` → 409 `"Packs can't be opened all at once yet."`;
      3. `pack_of`, `count_of` and `RequestKey::of(app, &req, "/api/packs/open-all")`;
      4. the registry, as `post_open` gets it;
      5. claim the turn;
      6. `count` × `SystemIds.seed()`;
      7. `open_packs_once(..).answer()`.
    - `app.rs`: a row right after `/api/packs/open`.

11. **`api/decks.rs` helpers.** Move each handler's body, after its id is read, into:
    - `save_deck(app: &App, profile_id: &str, id: &str, body: &Value) -> Result<DeckView, ApiError>`;
    - `save_trio -> TrioView`;
    - `remove_deck` and `remove_trio -> bool`.

    The four handlers call them and answer as they do now.

12. **Sync helpers.**
    - `fn sync_list<'b>(body, key) -> Result<&'b [Value], ApiError>`: absent or null is an empty list; anything but a list is 400.
    - `fn sync_answer(id: Value, outcome: Result<Value, ApiError>) -> Result<Value, ApiError>`:
      - `Ok` → the answer plus `"id"`;
      - `status() >= 500` → `Err`: the whole request fails, and the items already saved are idempotent on retry;

    - Read the lists `decks`, `trios`, `deletedTrios` and `deletedDecks`. More than `DECK_SYNC_ITEMS_MAX` items in all → 400, with nothing run.

    - `app.rs`: a row right after `DELETE /api/decks/:id`.

      - `DeckSyncRefusal = { id; status; error: ApiErrorBody }`.
      - `DeckSyncResponse`.
    - **`syncDecks(token, input, options = {})`:**
      - It is `apiRequest("/api/decks/sync", { method: "POST", token, body: input, ...options })`.
      - Saves fold with `withItem`.
      - Deck deletions fold with `withoutDeck`, extracted from `deleteDeck`.
      - Trio deletions fold by filter.

15. **`PackOpening.tsx`.**
    - `SceneState.all = count > 1`.
    - Add `queued = useRef<OpenedPackResponse[]>([])`, cleared by `start` and `close`.
    - `tear()`:
      - first try `queued.current.shift()`, which sends no request;
      - otherwise, after `spendOutNow()`, call `openAllPacks(token, pack, scene.left + 1)` when `all`, else `openPack`;
      - on success: queue the rest, `setOpened(first)`, fold only the last opening (`withOpening`, `onChanged`), and set `spent.current = true`.
    - `PacksHeld`: use `Math.min(count, PACKS_OPEN_ALL_MAX)` for both `onOpen` and the label.

16. **`sync.ts`.**

## Risks

- **Ledger order:** rows are inserted `order by n` over all the openings' grants in sequence, so each ledger matches N single opens. The only difference is one `at` for the whole batch. Both stores prove it.
- **Postgres-only bugs:** problems in the update/insert split or the gating CTEs show only in `db/run.sh`, so run it.
- **Determinism:** the seeds stay the server's, `count` only bounds the batch, and the fold mirrors the writes. No engine or shared code changes.
- **Transaction aborts:** a `raise` in `app.upsert_*` aborts a whole Postgres transaction, so the sync uses one transaction per item.
- **Client:** the panels take the batch's last answer, since its values are absolute (R3211000). `keepalive` bodies stay under 64 KB at 30 items.
- **Route tests:** the lists in `packs.rs` and `decks.rs` must match the order in `app.rs`.
